speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your systemic hypertension, can you tell me if you have any family history of high blood pressure or kidney disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Since he has no family history and is otherwise healthy, do you notice him having any headaches, dizziness, or vision changes recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a critical finding; a blood pressure discrepancy between limbs can indicate coarctation of the aorta. Please have the patient lie down while I perform a focused cardiovascular exam, listening carefully for faint or delayed femoral pulses compared to the brachial pulses. During this exam, I will also palpate the abdomen to check for any abdominal bruit.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta
